name: Chinese unification
summary: Chinese unification, as Beijing advances it, holds that Taiwan is an inseparable part of China and that the division left by the civil war must end in national reunification, preferably peacefully under one country, two systems, with force reserved against secession. It ties reunification to national rejuvenation and treats the question as China's internal affair. It is a single-issue territorial doctrine and says little on economic, social or cultural questions.
scope: The People's Republic of China's official doctrine of national reunification with Taiwan, as set out in the Anti-Secession Law (2005), the 2000 and 2022 white papers, the one country, two systems policy and Xi Jinping's 2019 speech; the scholarship (Grossman and Zheng, GMF) describes it the same way. It excludes the Republic of China/KMT version, in which unification would come under the ROC, and pro-unification currents in Taiwan that differ from Beijing's formula.
